Reading · people around the world

1.1 Talk with a partner. Do you have friends from other countries? Where are they from?

Sherigingiz bilan gaplashing. Boshqa mamlakatlardan doʻstlaringiz bormi? Ular qayerdan?

Kalit soʻzlar

a language exchange til almashish ilovasi — odamlar oʻz tilini oʻrgatib, sizning tilingizni oʻrganadigan ilova

abroad chet elda, boshqa mamlakatda

shy uyatchan — yangi odamlar bilan jim

a neighbour qoʻshni — yoningizda yashaydigan odam

New Friends in Five Countries

My name is Diana and I am from Colombia. I am 26 years old and I am a nurse in a big hospital in Bogotá. My job is difficult but interesting. In my free time, I am always on a language exchange app because my dream is to work abroad.

Now I have four good friends on the app, and they are all from different countries. Tomo is from Japan. He is a taxi driver in Osaka. He is very funny, but he says he is shy in English lessons. Marta and Paulo are married. They are from Brazil, and they are teachers in a small town near São Paulo. Their students are children, so questions are never a problem — my questions are easy for them!

My fourth friend is Amira. She is Egyptian, but she is not in Egypt now. She is a student in Germany, and her German neighbours are her “second family”. Amira's English is excellent, and she is a very kind teacher to me.

We are all very different: our countries, our jobs and our ages. But we are not strangers now — we are real friends, and English is our shared language.

4

Everyday English · asking for information

4.1 Read the conversation. Rustam is at a language school reception.

Suhbatni oʻqing. Rustam til maktabining qabulxonasida.

Receptionist Good morning! How can I help you?

Rustam Good morning. I'm here for the English course. My name's Rustam Karimov.

Receptionist Sorry, can you repeat your surname, please?

Rustam Karimov. K-A-R-I-M-O-V.

Receptionist Thank you. And where are you from, Rustam?

Rustam I'm from Uzbekistan — from Samarkand.

Receptionist Great. What's your phone number?

Rustam It's 90 315 22 48.

Receptionist Sorry, is that 22 or 32?

Rustam 22. Double two.

Receptionist Perfect. You're in Room 4. Welcome to the school!

4.2 Find in the conversation…

Suhbatdan toping…

1 two phrases for checking information

2 the question about a person's country

3 what Rustam does when his surname isn't clear

Foydali iboralar

Soʻrash: What's your name / surname? · How do you spell that? · Where are you from?

Tekshirish: Sorry, can you repeat that? · Sorry, is that 22 or 32? · So that's K-A-R-I-M-O-V, right?

5

Speaking

5.1 Role-play. Student A works at a gym, a school or a hotel. Student B is a new customer.

Rolli oʻyin. A oʻquvchi sport zalida, maktabda yoki mehmonxonada ishlaydi. B oʻquvchi — yangi mijoz. Buni sinfda bajarasiz.

Ask for: full name (and spelling) · country or city · phone number · email. Then change roles.

Esda tuting

Qabul xodimi ikkita javobni tekshirishi (Sorry, is that…?) va doʻstona gap bilan tugatishi kerak.

6

Writing · about you and your people

6.1 Write 6–8 sentences about you and two people in your life.

Oʻzingiz va hayotingizdagi ikki kishi haqida 6–8 ta gap yozing.

Use be in the positive and negative · one country or nationality word · three adjectives.

Model

My name is Karim and I am 24 years old. I am from Samarkand, and I am a student. I am not shy, but I am quiet in big groups. My best friend is Timur. He is funny and very clever. My sister is a doctor. Her job is difficult, but she is never tired. We are a small family, but we are very friendly.
